meta.title: Open 3D Viewer Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Free, open-source viewer for building models: open SketchUp, Tekla, Revit, IFC, glTF, CityJSON and more, measure, cut sections and save as IFC 4. For Windows, macOS, Linux and the browser.

header.label: 3D viewer for construction
header.title: Open 3D Viewer Studio
header.tagline: Free viewer to open, measure and section building models
header.desc: Open models from SketchUp, Tekla, Revit and IFC without the program they were made in. Orbit around them, measure, cut the model open and save it as IFC. As a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux, or right in the browser.
header.heroAlt: Open 3D Viewer Studio with a SketchUp model of a house on its plot, the layers on the left and the file properties on the right

notice.text: Try it right away: open your own model in the browser. The file stays on your own computer and is never uploaded. IFC and Revit open in the desktop app.

features.label: Features
features.heading: View, measure and pass on any model
features.sub: Start with the highlights, or pick a topic.

open.title: Opens what you are sent
open.desc: SketchUp, Tekla, Revit, IFC, glTF, OBJ, STL, PLY, CityJSON, LandXML and DWG or DXF, without the program the model was made in. The File page keeps your recent files at hand, so you can pick up right where you left off.
open.alt: The File page with Open, Save as, Settings and three recently opened SketchUp models

revit.title: Revit models with their schedules
revit.desc: The desktop app opens .rvt and .rfa with levels, grids, rooms and saved views, and IFC models with their spaces in a layer of their own. A schedule, such as a door schedule, opens as a table below the model; click a row and its elements are selected.
revit.alt: A Revit model with the door schedule as a table below the 3D view, the saved views on the left and the levels on the right

view.title: See the model the way you want
view.desc: Switch between solid, wireframe and edges, and between perspective and orthographic. Turn to a side with the view cube or look straight down, and switch layers on or off in the explorer.
view.alt: A house on its plot seen straight from above as a wireframe, with an orthographic camera and the dark theme

explode.title: See how it fits together
explode.desc: Pull the model apart per storey or per element, with a slider per axis. Cut it open with a section box or a section plane with filled cuts, and measure distances, angles, areas and polygons.
explode.alt: A bathroom model pulled apart per element, with the X, Y and Z sliders in the properties pane

workspace.title: A workspace you already know
workspace.desc: The window follows the OpenAEC Blueprint, like the other OpenAEC apps: a ribbon with Home, View and Measure, an explorer, properties and a status bar. Choose from five themes, work in English or Dutch and give every command your own shortcut.
workspace.alt: The same house model in four of the five themes: Light, Dark, Blueprint and High contrast dark

skp.title: SketchUp
skp.desc: Open .skp files from version 3 onwards, with the tags as layers.

tekla.title: Tekla Structures (beta)
tekla.desc: Open .db1 models, with a layer per class. Profile shapes are approximated.

ifc.title: IFC
ifc.desc: Open .ifc in the desktop app. Spaces sit in a layer of their own and start hidden, so you see the building right away.

revit.title: Revit
revit.desc: Open .rvt and .rfa in the desktop app, with levels, grids, rooms, saved views and schedules.

exchange.title: glTF, OBJ, STL and PLY
exchange.desc: The common exchange formats for 3D models, scans and 3D printing, in the browser too.

city.title: CityJSON and LandXML
city.desc: City models from CityJSON and CityJSONSeq, and terrain as a TIN from LandXML.

cad.title: DWG and DXF
cad.desc: The faces from model space, as 3D geometry. Not a full CAD drawing: solids, text and curves are not included.

multi.title: Several models at once
multi.desc: Open replaces the model, Add puts another file next to it. Every model has its own toggle to show or hide it.

modes.title: Solid, wireframe or edges
modes.desc: Change the display with a single key, and switch between perspective and orthographic.

cube.title: View cube and standard views
cube.desc: Turn to a side with the view cube, or choose iso, top, front or right. Press F to fit the model in view.

explode.title: Explode
explode.desc: Pull the model apart per storey or per element, with a slider per axis.

explorer.title: Explorer and properties
explorer.desc: Switch layers on or off, search the explorer and click an element to read its properties.

schedule.title: Revit schedules
schedule.desc: A schedule opens as a table below the model. Click a row and the matching elements are selected.

measure.title: Distances and angles
measure.desc: Measure by clicking in the model, or between two elements. Measurements stay in view until you clear them.

area.title: Areas and polygons
area.desc: Measure an area or a polygon over several points, such as a floor or a roof face.

section.title: Section box and section plane
section.desc: Cut the model open with a box or a single plane. The cuts are filled, so you can see what is solid.

ifcexport.title: Save as IFC 4
ifcexport.desc: Save any model you open as IFC 4, with storeys, classes, properties and materials. In the browser too.

mcp.title: Driven by AI
mcp.desc: With the open-3d-viewer-mcp MCP server, an AI assistant operates the desktop viewer, locally on your own computer.

browser.title: In the browser too
browser.desc: The same app runs in the browser on WebGPU. Your file stays on your computer and is not uploaded.

themes.title: Five themes, two languages
themes.desc: Light, Dark, Blueprint and two high-contrast themes, in English or Dutch.

shortcuts.title: Your own shortcuts
shortcuts.desc: Give every command your own key in Settings.

recent.title: Recent files
recent.desc: The File page shows the models you opened last, so you can carry on right away.

signed.title: Signed installers
signed.desc: For Windows, macOS and Linux, with checksums and a build attestation for every file.

whatsnew.label: New in v2026.44.17
whatsnew.title: A new window and more formats
whatsnew.desc: Open 3D Viewer Studio has been rebuilt in Rust and now follows the OpenAEC Blueprint. Revit and IFC open in the regular desktop app, new formats were added, you can view several models at once and the installers are signed. The full list is in the release notes.

blueprint.title: The OpenAEC window
blueprint.desc: Title bar, ribbon, a File page with recent files, explorer, properties and status bar, as in every OpenAEC app.

desktop.title: Revit and IFC on the desktop
desktop.desc: .rvt, .rfa and .ifc open in the regular desktop app.

schedules.title: Revit schedules
schedules.desc: A schedule opens as a table below the model, and a row selects its elements.

formats.title: CityJSON, LandXML and DWG/DXF
formats.desc: City models, terrain as a TIN and the faces from the model space of a drawing.

multi.title: Several models at once
multi.desc: Combine files in one view and show or hide each model separately.

signed.title: Signed installers
signed.desc: For Windows, macOS and Linux, with checksums and a build attestation for every file.

files.a: On the desktop and in the browser: SketchUp (.skp, version 3 and later), Tekla Structures (.db1, beta), glTF and GLB, Wavefront OBJ, STL, PLY, CityJSON and CityJSONSeq, terrain as a TIN from LandXML, and DWG and DXF (only the faces from model space, not a full CAD drawing). Only in the desktop app: IFC (.ifc) and Revit (.rvt, .rfa), with levels, grids, rooms, saved views and schedules.

install.q: Do I need to install anything?
install.a: No. Open 3D Viewer Studio also runs in the browser, on WebGPU, and your file is not uploaded. For IFC and Revit you need the desktop app, for Windows, macOS or Linux. The OpenAEC Installer installs and updates all your OpenAEC apps in one go.

price.q: What does Open 3D Viewer Studio cost?
price.a: Nothing. The app is free and open source under the LGPL-3.0-or-later. No subscription, no account and no per-user license fees.

save.q: In which file format is my work saved?
save.a: Save as creates an IFC 4 file, on the desktop and in the browser. The geometry is saved as triangles (IfcTriangulatedFaceSet), with the storeys, classes, properties and materials of the model. That way you can turn a SketchUp or Tekla model into IFC, for example. The original file stays as it was.

systems.q: Which systems does it run on?
systems.a: Windows 10 and 11 (x64), macOS 11 or later (universal: Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux (x86-64, as .deb, .rpm, AppImage or .tar.gz). And in any browser with WebGPU. The window is in English and Dutch.

practice.q: Does it fit the way construction works?
practice.a: Yes. It opens the models that architects, engineers and builders exchange, from SketchUp and Tekla to Revit and IFC, as well as city models in CityJSON and terrain from LandXML. Whatever you open, you can save as IFC 4, the open standard for BIM.

ai.q: What can an AI assistant do with it?
ai.a: With the MCP server open-3d-viewer-mcp (Model Context Protocol, an open standard), an AI assistant such as Claude Code, Claude Desktop or another MCP client operates the desktop viewer the way you do: opening files, looking around, selecting, reading properties, cutting sections and measuring. You see it happen in your own window. Everything stays on your computer: the viewer only listens on 127.0.0.1, with a token.

multi.q: Can I view several models at once?
multi.a: Yes. Open replaces the model you are viewing; Add puts another file next to it, for example the structure next to the architecture. Every model has its own toggle to show or hide it. IFC spaces sit in a layer of their own and start hidden.

limits.q: What can it not do yet?
limits.a: IFC and Revit open only in the desktop app. Textures become an average colour. Tekla profiles are approximated; that reader is still in beta. From DWG and DXF only the faces come along, without ACIS solids, text, dimensions and curves. And the browser version does not respond while a large model is loading.

verify.q: How do I know the download is genuine?
verify.a: The installers are signed: Windows with Authenticode, macOS with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple, Linux with the OpenAEC OpenPGP key (fingerprint 13F6 D414 ADEE 4ED4 CD09 AC60 601D 86C9 3C50 4D29). Every release includes SHA256SUMS and its signature SHA256SUMS.asc, and every file has a GitHub build attestation.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: For those who want to know how it is built.

rust.title: Rust
rust.desc: One Rust code base for the desktop app and the browser version.

iced.title: iced
iced.desc: The interface is built with iced, a GUI library in Rust, without a web view or JavaScript framework.

wgpu.title: Own renderer on wgpu
wgpu.desc: An own 3D pipeline on wgpu with 4x anti-aliasing: native on the desktop, on WebGPU in the browser.

wasm.title: WebAssembly
wasm.desc: In the browser the same code runs as WebAssembly. Models are read locally; nothing goes to a server.

blueprint.title: OpenAEC Blueprint
blueprint.desc: Window, design tokens, fonts and icons come from the OpenAEC Blueprint, the standard for all OpenAEC apps.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.desc: open-3d-viewer-mcp connects an MCP client to the window, only through 127.0.0.1 and with a token.

formats.label: File formats
formats.title: What opens where
formats.desc: The desktop app opens every format. In the browser everything opens except IFC and Revit, and saving as IFC 4 works in both.
